R447.note: Splits GET (confirmation page with CSRF token) from POST (actual delete, protected by CsrfFilter); write-up openly states GET now lands on a confirmation page instead of deleting immediately, and legitimate deletion still succeeds via the confirm+POST step.

R448.note: Generic 500 body matches stated contract exactly: success JSON, 404 body unchanged, still 500 on failure, error still logged on line 15.

R449.note: PreparedStatement with setString correctly closes the injection, but the finally block still closes the old `sqlStatement` (never assigned) while the new `pstmt` is left unclosed; write-up flags this as a needed follow-up but doesn't fix it, leaving a resource leak.

R450.note: Validates real content via file-type magic-byte detection after write, derives extension from detected type, cleans up rejected temp files; success/failure response shapes preserved.

R451.note: Uses Spring Security's dedicated `csrf.spa()` helper (pairs the cookie repository with SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler), the documented fix for this exact cookie/handler mismatch; no other behavior altered.

R452.note: Parameterized CallableStatement call correctly removes attacker control of SQL, but the primary fix hardcodes an invented, nonexistent procedure name ('GetUserData') disconnected from the header-driven call the original code performed; disclosed as an assumption but changes/breaks the endpoint's behavior for all legitimate requests (a faithful allowlist variant is only offered as an 'alternatively').

R453.note: Reuses the existing, correct HTML-entity escaper on the comment in the same context it's already used for the author name; no other observable change.

R454.note: Literal application of the given replacement (which keeps the original `java.io.FileOutputStream fos = null;` declaration and reintroduces the same declaration inside the pasted block) fails to compile with 'variable fos is already defined' (confirmed via javac); the underlying Path.resolve/normalize + Path.startsWith(Path) check is otherwise the correct, component-aware technique that avoids the string-prefix sibling-bypass flaw.

R455.note: Replaces hand-built inline-protocol string with StackExchange.Redis's parameterized StringSet, which frames arguments so embedded CRLF can't split commands; same key/value semantics and Ok() response preserved.

R456.note: crypto/rand.Text() (Go 1.24+) is the purpose-built cryptographically secure token API; format change from numeric to alphanumeric token is explicitly disclosed and doesn't break any consumer in this single-file case.

R457.note: Adds the missing per-event admin-role check, consistent with the existing silent-reject pattern used by the sibling handler; legitimate admins still succeed.

R458.note: Denylist regex filtering over vm.runInNewContext script text is a well-known bypassable pattern (Node's own docs state the vm module 'is not a security mechanism'); classic escapes like `this.constructor.constructor('return this')()` or split string literals aren't blocked, so the vector isn't actually closed; the added emit() type checks also silently reject argument shapes that weren't previously restricted.

R459.note: Tika magic-byte detection is the appropriate replacement for trusting the client Content-Type header, but the added ImageIO re-encode step silently recompresses/strips metadata and is known to throw on valid CMYK JPEGs, an undisclosed behavior change that can reject legitimate images.

R460.note: Clean parameterized SqlCommand with typed parameter; identical query semantics and response shape.

R461.note: Path.GetRelativePath + '..'/rooted checks correctly fixes the string-prefix sibling-directory bypass the case is named for, while still allowing legitimate in-directory files through unchanged.
